# Somanassa Sutta (Iti 37 (It 2.10 PTS It 29))

**ID:** Iti 37 (It 2.10 PTS It 29)

**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Somanassa Sutta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Somanassa Sutta* (Iti 37) is a short discourse in the *Dukanipāta* (Book of the Twos) of the *Itivuttaka* (PTS It 29–30) [Piya Tan 2004]. Its central theme is religious urgency (*saṁvega*) and its practical fruits: the text teaches that when endowed with two qualities—a keen sense of urgency and appropriate exertion—a monastic dwells in great mental ease and happiness in the present life (*diṭṭhe va dhamme somanassavihārī*) while wisely rousing effort toward the destruction of the mental defilements or influxes (*āsavānaṁ khayāya*) [Piya Tan 2004].
